content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make a documentary when travelling, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Design the visual aesthetic and color palette (4 days)
Step 2. Research local historical archives (1 week)
Step 3. Record the final voiceover narration (2 days)
Step 4. Conduct on-camera interviews with local experts (3 days)
Step 5. Draft the initial narrative outline (5 days)
Step 6. Apply for international filming permits (2 months)
Step 7. Mix the final audio and sound effects (1 week)
Step 8. Color grade the final assembly (10 days)
Step 9. Create promotional social media teasers (2 days)
Step 10. Edit the final director's cut (3 weeks)
Step 11. Secure music licensing rights (2 weeks)

Step 15. Inventory and pack camera gear (1 day)
Step 16. Film establishing shots of the landscape (5 days)
Step 17. Write the final script based on footage (1 week)
Step 18. Rent high-end lenses and stabilizers (3 days)
Step 19. Define the documentary's core message (4 days)
Step 20. Master the film for theatrical release (3 days)
Step 21. Secure funding and sponsorships (3 months)
Step 22. Book flights and accommodation (2 days)
Step 23. Brainstorm the central concept (1 week)
Step 24. Hire a professional cinematographer (10 days)
Step 25. Export the final high-resolution file (5 hours)
Step 26. Create a storyboard for key scenes (1 week)

Step 30. Design the opening title sequence (3 days)
Step 31. Record foley sound effects (4 days)
Step 32. Organize the digital footage library (2 days)
Step 33. Submit the film to festivals (1 day)
Step 34. Translate and time-code subtitles (1 week)
Step 35. Host a private premiere for the crew (1 day)
Step 36. Create a detailed shooting schedule (4 days)
Step 37. Edit the rough cut of the film (1 month)

Step 39. Develop a character list (3 days)
Step 40. Select the best interview takes (5 days)
Step 41. Purchase a durable travel laptop (1 day)
Step 42. Conduct technical rehearsals (2 days)
Step 43. Film the primary action sequences (2 weeks)
Step 44. Review daily footage for quality (12 hours)

Step 46. Buy a set of high-speed memory cards (3 hours)
Step 47. Log and transcribe all interviews (1 week)
Step 48. Sign non-disclosure agreements with crew (1 day)
Step 49. Interview local residents for B-roll (4 days)
Step 50. Record local street musicians for the score (2 days)

Step 52. Sync the audio and video tracks (3 days)
Step 53. Record an "on-the-road" video diary (1 week)
Step 54. Archive the project project files (2 days)
Step 55. Arrange local transportation for the crew (4 days)
Step 56. Capture time-lapse sequences (3 days)
Step 57. Assemble the first assembly of clips (1 week)
Step 58. Identify potential interview subjects (1 week)
Step 59. Set the project budget (5 days)
Step 60. Capture B-roll of local landmarks (4 days)
Step 61. Hire a production assistant (1 week)
Step 62. Choose a video editing software (1 day)
Step 63. Record the "A-roll" narrative footage (5 days)
Step 64. Buy weather-proof gear covers (2 days)
Step 65. Select a temporary working title (1 day)
Step 66. Capture drone aerial footage (2 days)
Step 67. Clear storage on all mobile devices (2 hours)
Step 68. Create a project mood board (3 days)
Step 69. Write the interview questions (2 days)
Step 70. Edit a three-minute trailer (4 days)
Step 71. Perform a final data integrity check (6 hours)
Step 72. Prepare the press kit (3 days)
Step 73. Create the end credit scroll (2 days)
Step 74. Create a marketing plan (1 week)
Step 75. Research the political climate of the destination (5 days)
Step 76. Apply for a business credit card (1 week)
Step 77. Organize the "selects" reel (3 days)
Step 78. Finalize the travel itinerary (4 days)
Step 79. Create a digital assembly of all assets (2 days)
Step 80. Commission an original theme song (2 weeks)
Step 81. Film the introduction segment (1 day)
Step 82. Purchase a portable power station (1 day)
Step 83. Calibrate the camera sensors (2 hours)
Step 84. Inspect all cables and connectors (4 hours)
Step 85. Script the transition scenes (3 days)
Step 86. Build a website for the film (5 days)
Step 87. Hire a sound recordist (1 week)
Step 88. Register the production company (1 month)
Step 89. Plan the distribution strategy (1 week)
Step 90. Record natural wildlife sounds (3 days)
